summary: Provisioning hang caused by orphaned udev rule from USB dongle firmware update
summary_extended: Multiple provisioning jobs for returned/repaired laptops are hanging during the post-image checkin stage. Investigation points to a udev rule left behind by a vendor USB management tool that triggers a blocking call in the provisioning agent when the device is present.
impact: Blocking autopilot-style provisioning in staging for ~6% of depot-return devices. Slows depot throughput and prevents automatic re-enrollment; potential customer-impact if regression reaches prod.
environment_notes: Observed in staging-us-east image pipeline. Repro rate higher on devices that previously received vendor dongle firmware update (security tokens used in corporate field repair workflow). Affected devices boot to Windows PE then the provisioning agent runs and stalls at hardware enumeration step.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Take a repaired laptop that previously had vendor security dongle attached. 2) Flash latest vendor dongle firmware using vendor tool. 3) Wipe and image device via depot imaging pipeline. 4) Wait for provisioning agent to perform hardware checks — process stalls during udev/driver enumeration and provisioning does not progress.
observed_logs:
Provisioning-agent log snippet:
[2026-03-08 09:12:03] provisioning-agent: start hardware-check
[2026-03-08 09:12:03] provisioning-agent: enumerate-blocking-drivers
[2026-03-08 09:12:03] udev: found rule 99-vendor-token.rules -> executing handler '/usr/local/bin/vendor-token-probe'
[2026-03-08 09:12:03] vendor-token-probe: waiting for HSM init (timeout suppressed)
... (no further progress)
investigation_notes:
- Reproduced locally with a test token: vendor probe script enters a blocking wait for token initialization when run by system user in provisioning context.
- The vendor's MSIX installer drops a udev rule in /etc/udev/rules.d/99-vendor-token.rules that invokes /usr/local/bin/vendor-token-probe on add events.
- In depot images the provisioning agent triggers a udev enumerate which fires the rule; vendor-token-probe expects interactive environment and hangs.
- Temporary workaround: remove the udev rule before running provisioning agent or override probe script to exit quickly if run as 'provisioning-agent' user.
- Root cause: vendor firmware flash tool bundles a hardware integration package that was not removed during field repair; our imaging sequence does not always scrub third-party udev entries when wiping user space artifacts on returned units.
mitigation_attempts: 1) Manual removal of /etc/udev/rules.d/99-vendor-token.rules allowed provisioning to complete. 2) Updated staging image to include udev rule cleanup hook; short-term patch applied to depot 'pre-imaging cleanup' script. 3) Created a feature flag in provisioning-agent to ignore udev-triggered handlers when running in automated depot context.
workaround: Run 'rm /etc/udev/rules.d/99-vendor-token.rules' in pre-imaging hook or boot to WinPE and use our depot cleanup script prior to starting provisioning agent.
proposed_fix: 1) Add a robust cleanup step to depot imaging that removes third-party udev rules and vendor probe binaries. 2) Update provisioning-agent to run udev enumeration under a filtered environment that does not trigger external handlers. 3) Open vendor support case to request an updated firmware package that does not drop a blocking probe script or to document safe uninstall steps.
risk_and_rollback: Low risk for imaging pipeline if cleanup runs; provisioning-agent feature-flag change is reversible. Vendor engagement may take longer — we'll maintain cleanup script until vendor releases updated package.
next_steps: - (Liam) finalize and land pre-imaging cleanup patch to staging by 2026-03-11. - (Priya) open vendor support ticket and attach logs by 2026-03-10. - (Eng Ops) schedule a canary where 5% of depot images run the cleanup hook for 48 hours. - (SRE) add alert to detect provisioning stalls >10m during hardware-check.
